key_insight: MedHiVE models anatomical hierarchies in both 3D scans and reports to learn aligned local and global representations.
clinical_relevance: Anatomy-aware representations could support medical image segmentation, classification, and detection, though clinical utility remains unestablished.
method: Routes image and text tokens through local and global Soft Mixture-of-Experts layers.
Uses report-derived anatomical supervision to align anatomy-level and whole-scan representations.
Combines hierarchical token routing with contrastive vision-language learning.
evidence_signal: Pre-trained on 25,000+ CT scans with anatomical supervision, MedHiVE reportedly outperformed 11 state-of-the-art methods across 6 datasets covering segmentation, classification, and detection.
watch_item: The abstract does not report effect sizes or prospective clinical validation, limiting assessment of practical benefit.
paper_title: Multimodal Hierarchical Mixture-of-Experts for 3D Medical Vision-Language Modeling
